$comment: RLS-9 ratchet (scripts/audit-rls-surface.ts). Call sites that read or write an RLS-covered table without a threaded transaction. The gate fails BOTH for an unlisted finding and for a listed entry whose count drops or disappears, so every entry is a deliberate, reviewable act with a diagnosed reason. Never add one merely to go green — see the header of scripts/audit-rls-surface.ts.
$baseline: 2026-08-25 — 34 sites, seeded from a LINE-ENDING-NORMALISED scan. The first CI run disagreed with the local one (32 vs 34): several detectors inspect a fixed CHARACTER window (400 chars after a call, 900 either side of db.execute), and CRLF costs one extra char per line, so a window spans fewer LINES on a Windows checkout than on Linux CI. The script now normalises CRLF before scanning, so both platforms agree. Most entries are RLS-8's worklist, NOT absolution; two are verified false positives and are labelled as such.
$howToTriage: Three legitimate outcomes per entry: (1) scope it — thread `tx` or wrap in withCurrentTenant; (2) route it through the RLS-6/RLS-7 adminDb path if it is a deliberate cross-tenant admin read; (3) keep it and document why, if it is a bootstrap path that must run before a tenant is known (token-authenticated lookups, login by email). Detection is TEXTUAL, so a false positive is also a valid reason — record that too.

allow.reason: Bare db.transaction() on the authentication path, which runs before a tenant is known. Should become withCurrentTenant only if a tenant is genuinely available there. Tracked by RLS-8.
Bare db.transaction() during block execution; a tenant context should be ambient here, so this likely wants withCurrentTenant. Tracked by RLS-8.
audit_logs write. Audit writes must not fail closed or an audited action becomes unauditable; needs a deliberate decision on whether it scopes or bypasses. Tracked by RLS-8.
Direct db.* on datavault_databases, which carries a policy. Highest-count db-call site; needs threading through the caller's transaction. Tracked by RLS-8.
Tenant bootstrap/lookup path that may legitimately run before a tenant GUC is set. Triage under RLS-8.
Analytics read on a covered table outside a tenant transaction. Under enforcement this returns empty rather than erroring, which is the silent shape — scope it. Tracked by RLS-8.
Same audit-write consideration as auditLogger.ts; decide both together under RLS-8.
Authentication path, pre-tenant by nature. Same reasoning as auth.routes.ts. Confirm under RLS-8.

MFA secrets/backup codes are keyed to the user, not the tenant, and are read during authentication before a tenant context exists. Probable keep-and-document; confirm the tables involved actually carry policies under RLS-8.

Snapshot reads/writes touch covered tables outside a tenant transaction. Related to WorkflowClonerService's cross-tenant admin path noted in RLS-4 precondition notes; decide scope-vs-adminDb under RLS-8.

FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-08-25. The call at line 639 is `db.select().from(templates)`, and `templates` has NO policy — it was deliberately removed from RLS_REPOS as a false positive (see this script's header). The db-call detector scans 400 chars after the call for a covered table name and catches `activeWorkflows`/`pinnedWorkflows` six lines below. Only surfaces on LF checkouts, where the window spans more lines — which is how it slipped past the Windows-seeded baseline.
Runs inside workflow execution, where a tenant context should already exist — likely needs the ambient context threading rather than a new scope. Tracked by RLS-8.
sli_configs / sli_windows are covered tables read by service-level indicator reporting, which is cross-tenant by design. Candidate for the adminDb path. Tracked by RLS-8.
Run-state read/write on a covered table; run paths are token-authenticated and may bootstrap before a tenant is resolved. Triage under RLS-8.

Raw db.execute() whose SQL names a covered table. raw-execute is the widest net and the most false-positive-prone detector — verify the query actually touches a policy table before converting. Tracked by RLS-8.
Raw analytics SQL naming a covered table. Same verify-before-converting caveat as UserRepository. Tracked by RLS-8.

FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-08-25. Both db.execute() calls query `workflow_run_events`, which carries NO policy — it is not in COVERED_TABLES_SQL and has no CREATE POLICY in any migration. The raw-execute detector looks 900 chars either side of the call, and that window catches the word `workflows` from neighbouring SQL. Kept listed rather than narrowing the window, because a tighter window trades a false positive for a false negative, and this detector is the last line of defence for raw SQL. Re-verify if the query changes.

Public (unauthenticated) portal reads via db.query.<table>. These are token- or slug-authorised and run with no tenant context by design — the same shape as RLS-4 precondition 3. Probable keep-and-document; confirm under RLS-8.

Deliberately cross-tenant: findAllUsers / findAllUsersWithWorkflowCounts / findAttributedToUser serve the platform admin console. Must be routed through the RLS-6 adminDb bypass path, NOT scoped — scoping would truncate the console to the acting admin's own tenant, which is the silent failure RLS-6 exists to prevent. Tracked by RLS-8.

Authentication bootstrap: the identifying lookup runs before any tenant is known, so there is no tenant to scope to. Migration 0032 (rls_login_email_bootstrap) exists precisely to let this read succeed under enforcement. Likely a keep-and-document outcome; confirm under RLS-8.
1 unthreaded site out of 27 — the file threads tx nearly everywhere, so this is a single missed call rather than an unscoped design. Straightforward fix under RLS-8.
